events.title: US government auctions seized Silk Road bitcoin

research.summary: The US Marshals Service auctioned 29,656 BTC forfeited from Silk Road infrastructure on 27 June 2014.
research.significance: A government auction of seized Bitcoin was an extraordinary early moment in which law enforcement treated BTC as a sellable asset rather than merely contraband.

sources.title: Bitcoin historical auction record — USMS June 2014

events.title: Realcoin/Tether origins

research.summary: The stablecoin project began in 2014 under the Realcoin name and was renamed Tether; the first USDT tokens were issued on 6 October 2014 on the Bitcoin/Omni layer.
research.significance: Tether became the dominant crypto-native dollar instrument and one of the most consequential pieces of exchange infrastructure in crypto history.

sources.title: Tether — Eight Years of Stability and Innovation

events.title: Ethereum is publicly unveiled

research.summary: Ethereum was publicly introduced in January 2014, with Vitalik Buterin publishing the 'Ethereum: Now Going Public' post and presenting the project at the North American Bitcoin Conference in Miami.
research.significance: The public unveiling turned Ethereum from a circulated proposal into an organized project seeking developers, funding and users.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Ethereum: Now Going Public

events.title: Ethereum Yellow Paper formalizes the protocol

research.summary: Ethereum's official timeline dates Gavin Wood's Yellow Paper to 1 April 2014.
research.significance: The Yellow Paper gave Ethereum a formal technical specification and defined the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

events.title: Counterparty expands token experimentation on Bitcoin

research.summary: Counterparty was publicly launched on 2 January 2014, with XCP distributed through a proof-of-burn mechanism on Bitcoin.
research.significance: Counterparty showed that tokens, assets and later collectibles could be built on Bitcoin years before the modern NFT boom.

events.title: Newsweek claims to identify Satoshi Nakamoto

research.summary: Newsweek published a cover story identifying Dorian Prentice Satoshi Nakamoto as Bitcoin's creator. Dorian denied involvement, and the claim was not substantiated.
research.significance: The media frenzy became one of the most famous failed attempts to unmask Satoshi and highlighted the privacy stakes around Bitcoin's creator.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dorian Nakamoto denies Bitcoin involvement

research.notes: Record explicitly as a disputed/failed identification, never as fact that Dorian was Satoshi.

events.title: Microsoft begins accepting Bitcoin for some digital purchases

research.summary: Microsoft began allowing US customers to add Bitcoin-funded credit for purchases in the Windows and Xbox stores.
research.significance: A global technology company accepting Bitcoin represented a major merchant-adoption milestone.

sources.title: Ars Technica — Microsoft accepts Bitcoin for Xbox/Windows credit

events.title: Trezor brings an early consumer hardware wallet to market

research.summary: Trezor Model One officially launched on 29 July 2014 as the first commercial hardware wallet.
research.significance: Trezor created a new self-custody product category by isolating private keys from general-purpose computers.

sources.title: Trezor — 10 years since first hardware wallet

events.title: Dogecoin community funds the Jamaican bobsled team

research.summary: The Dogecoin community raised more than 26 million DOGE, worth roughly $25,000 at the time, to help the Jamaican bobsled team reach the Sochi Winter Olympics.
research.significance: The fundraiser proved that a joke cryptocurrency could mobilize a global internet community for real-world causes.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dogecoin Jamaican bobsled fundraiser

events.title: Dogecoin community sponsors NASCAR driver Josh Wise

research.summary: Reddit's Dogecoin community raised 67.8 million DOGE, about $55,000 at the time, to sponsor NASCAR driver Josh Wise; Dogecoin branding appeared on his car at Talladega and the community later helped him win the Sprint Fan Vote.
research.significance: The sponsorship turned Dogecoin's meme identity into one of crypto's most memorable mainstream-culture stunts.

sources.title: NASCAR — Josh Wise wins Sprint Fan Vote

events.title: Hal Finney dies, leaving a foundational Bitcoin legacy

research.summary: Hal Finney died on 28 August 2014 after living with ALS.
research.significance: Finney was a pioneering cypherpunk, creator of RPOW, early Bitcoin tester and recipient of the first Bitcoin transaction, giving his life story unique importance to crypto history.

events.title: Monero launches from CryptoNote roots

research.summary: The Monero blockchain went live on 18 April 2014 as a fair-launched CryptoNote-derived privacy cryptocurrency.
research.significance: Monero became the most enduring privacy-focused cryptocurrency and a central case in debates over fungibility, anonymity and regulation.

events.title: Stellar network launches

research.summary: Stellar publicly launched in July 2014, founded by Jed McCaleb and Joyce Kim with the Stellar Development Foundation.
research.significance: Stellar became a major payments-focused blockchain and an important branch of the Ripple/XRP family tree.

events.title: GHash.io approaches majority Bitcoin mining power

research.summary: GHash.io briefly exceeded or approached half of Bitcoin's network hash rate in June 2014, triggering intense concern over mining centralization and 51% attack risk.
research.significance: The episode became Bitcoin's clearest early warning about mining-pool concentration.

sources.title: SEC filing discussing GHash.io network share

events.title: OneCoin begins operations

research.summary: US investigators later established that OneCoin Ltd. was founded in or about April 2014 by Ruja Ignatova and another co-founder.
research.significance: OneCoin became one of the largest frauds marketed as cryptocurrency and is essential to crypto-scam history.

events.title: Tim Draper wins a large US Marshals auction of Silk Road Bitcoin

research.summary: Venture capitalist Tim Draper was publicly identified as the winning bidder for all roughly 29,656 BTC in the first US Marshals Silk Road auction.
research.significance: Draper's purchase became one of crypto's most famous institutional conviction stories and later contrasted sharply with government reserve policy.

sources.title: Bitcoin historical auction record — USMS June 2014

events.title: BitMEX is founded

research.summary: BitMEX began real-Bitcoin trading on 24 November 2014 after an earlier beta trading challenge.
research.significance: BitMEX became a major derivatives venue and helped popularize leveraged perpetual-swap trading in crypto.

events.title: Tether begins issuing dollar-linked tokens

research.summary: Tether's first USD₮ issuance occurred on 6 October 2014.
research.significance: Canonicalized under the Realcoin/Tether origin event.

sources.title: Tether — Eight Years of Stability and Innovation

events.title: Quantum by Kevin McCoy becomes an early blockchain-linked digital artwork

research.summary: Kevin McCoy's digital artwork Quantum was originally minted on the Namecoin blockchain on 3 May 2014.
research.significance: Quantum is one of the strongest early precedents for blockchain-linked digital art and later NFT culture.

events.title: Cryptsy grows into a major altcoin exchange before later collapse

research.summary: Cryptsy became a prominent altcoin exchange during the explosion of new coins, but this row describes market prominence rather than a single milestone.
research.significance: Use Cryptsy's later insolvency/collapse as the stronger canonical event.

events.title: Ethereum Name Service concept emerges from naming-system research

research.summary: The claim that the Ethereum Name Service concept 'emerged' in 2014 is too vague and predates the documented ENS launch work.
research.significance: Remove from card scoring; ENS's 2017 launch is the canonical milestone.

events.title: Mt. Gox halts withdrawals citing transaction malleability

research.summary: Mt. Gox halted Bitcoin withdrawals, publicly attributing problems to transaction malleability while deeper solvency issues were emerging.
research.significance: The withdrawal freeze was the immediate public warning before Mt. Gox's collapse.

sources.title: The Guardian — MtGox collapse / withdrawal halt analysis

events.title: Mt. Gox files for bankruptcy protection

research.summary: Mt. Gox filed for bankruptcy protection in Tokyo on 28 February 2014.
research.significance: Bankruptcy is a core subevent of the canonical Mt. Gox collapse.

events.title: Ethereum crowdsale raises funds using Bitcoin

research.summary: Ethereum's crowdsale accepted Bitcoin and raised tens of thousands of BTC in exchange for future ETH.
research.significance: This is the funding-mechanics context of the canonical Ether sale.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Launching the Ether Sale
Ethereum Foundation — Ether Sale statistical overview

events.title: Tether initially launches as Realcoin on Omni

research.summary: Realcoin/Tether used the Bitcoin-based Omni/Mastercoin layer for issuance.
research.significance: Technical context for the canonical Tether origin event.

sources.title: Tether — Eight Years of Stability and Innovation

events.title: Dogecoin community raises funds for water wells in Kenya

research.summary: The Doge4Water campaign raised about $31,997 for charity: water, including a roughly $30,439 Dogecoin-community donation.
research.significance: It demonstrated Dogecoin's early community philanthropy beyond its better-known bobsled and NASCAR campaigns.

events.title: PayPal announces limited Bitcoin integrations through partners

research.summary: PayPal announced relationships with BitPay, Coinbase and GoCoin so digital-goods merchants could accept Bitcoin through PayPal's payments ecosystem.
research.significance: The announcement was an early bridge between mainstream payment processing and cryptocurrency merchants.

sources.title: PayPal newsroom — PayPal and Virtual Currency

events.title: Counterparty launches decentralized asset issuance on Bitcoin

research.summary: Counterparty's proof-of-burn distribution created XCP and opened permissionless asset issuance on Bitcoin.
research.significance: Technical significance of the canonical Counterparty launch.

events.title: Namecoin identity and naming experiments continue beyond currency use

research.summary: Namecoin continued experimenting with decentralized names and identity-like uses beyond simple currency.
research.significance: Context under the 2011 Namecoin launch, not a distinct 2014 event.

events.title: XCoin launches, later becoming Darkcoin and Dash

research.summary: Evan Duffield launched the chain that became Dash on 18 January 2014. It was initially named XCoin, soon renamed Darkcoin, and later Dash.
research.significance: The project became an early privacy- and payments-focused altcoin and introduced the X11 mining algorithm.

events.title: Monero community takes over from Bytecoin/CryptoNote controversy

research.summary: After disagreement with the original founder, the Monero community and Core Team continued the project and rejected controversial proposed changes.
research.significance: The community takeover is an important governance-origin story within Monero's launch period.

events.title: Charlie Shrem is arrested over alleged unlicensed-money-transmission activity

research.summary: US prosecutors unsealed charges against BitInstant co-founder Charlie Shrem and Robert Faiella on 27 January 2014; Shrem had been arrested the prior day.
research.significance: The case was one of the first prominent criminal enforcement actions involving a well-known Bitcoin executive and money-transmission rules.

sources.title: US DOJ — Shrem and Faiella charges

events.title: Newsweek Dorian Nakamoto cover creates global Satoshi-media frenzy

research.summary: Newsweek's Dorian Nakamoto cover triggered a global media chase and controversy.
research.significance: Cultural/media context for the canonical disputed-identification event.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dorian Nakamoto denies Bitcoin involvement

events.title: Dorian Nakamoto denies creating Bitcoin

research.summary: Dorian Nakamoto denied any connection to Bitcoin after the Newsweek story.
research.significance: The denial immediately undermined the identification and became part of Satoshi lore.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dorian Nakamoto denies Bitcoin involvement

events.title: Satoshi-associated P2P Foundation account posts 'I am not Dorian Nakamoto'

research.summary: A post from the old Satoshi-associated P2P Foundation account stated 'I am not Dorian Nakamoto.'
research.significance: The message intensified the mystery, though account provenance alone cannot prove who authored it.

sources.title: The Guardian — Dorian Nakamoto denies Bitcoin involvement

research.notes: Attribute to the Satoshi-associated account; do not assert personal authorship.

events.title: Gavin Andresen becomes one of Bitcoin's most visible core maintainers

research.summary: Gavin Andresen became Bitcoin's most visible lead maintainer after Satoshi stepped away.
research.significance: Biographical/governance trend rather than one 2014 event; specific maintainer transitions are better candidates.

events.title: Bitcoin Core replaces Bitcoin-Qt branding

research.summary: Bitcoin's reference client was rebranded from Bitcoin-Qt toward the 'Bitcoin Core' name in December 2013; the 0.9.0 release followed in March 2014.
research.significance: The rebrand distinguished the Bitcoin network from one particular software implementation.

sources.title: Bitcoin development history — rebranding to Core

events.title: BitPay sponsors college football bowl game

research.summary: BitPay and ESPN Events announced a three-year deal creating the Bitcoin St. Petersburg Bowl, with the first game scheduled for 26 December 2014.
research.significance: It brought Bitcoin branding onto a nationally televised US college-football event and became a classic early mainstream-marketing moment.

sources.title: BitPay — ESPN and BitPay bowl partnership

events.title: Dish Network begins accepting Bitcoin

research.summary: DISH announced that it would become the largest company at the time to accept Bitcoin for subscription payments, with rollout planned for the third quarter.
research.significance: Another major US consumer brand added Bitcoin to mainstream merchant-adoption history.

sources.title: DISH newsroom — DISH to Accept Bitcoin

events.title: Dell begins accepting Bitcoin

research.summary: Dell.com began accepting Bitcoin from US consumers and small-business customers through Coinbase.
research.significance: At the time, Dell was described as the largest ecommerce company to officially accept Bitcoin.

events.title: PayPal Braintree announces Bitcoin support via Coinbase

research.summary: Braintree announced that developers would soon be able to integrate Bitcoin payments through a Coinbase partnership.
research.significance: The Braintree integration was a precursor to PayPal's broader virtual-currency merchant announcement later that month.

events.title: Coinbase launches merchant-processing integrations

research.summary: Coinbase expanded merchant-processing integrations during 2014, including major merchants such as Dell.
research.significance: Adoption context; individual merchant announcements make stronger standalone events.

events.title: Moolah and MintPal collapse adds to exchange-risk lore

research.summary: The Moolah/MintPal episode combined exchange ownership, operational failure and allegations around Moolah's operator.
research.significance: Composite lore row; it should be split only if a specific hack, acquisition or collapse milestone earns card consideration.
research.notes: Exclude from standalone scoring as written.

events.title: MintPal suffers a major hack

research.summary: MintPal suffered security and operational problems during 2014, but the raw row lacks a single fully sourced loss/date milestone.
research.significance: Retain as exchange-risk context; do not score independently unless narrowed.

events.title: US government restricts further production of funded Casascius coins

research.summary: Casascius creator Mike Caldwell stopped selling newly funded physical bitcoins after FinCEN contact in late 2013, not 2014.
research.significance: The episode shows early US money-transmission rules reaching physical bearer Bitcoin products.

events.title: Bitcoin Bowl brings crypto branding to US college football

research.summary: The Bitcoin St. Petersburg Bowl sponsorship and related BitPay branding were part of the same college-football marketing story.
research.significance: Likely duplicate/context of LORE-EVT-0680 once the sponsorship announcement is precisely sourced.

events.title: GHash.io voluntarily reduces mining share after 51 percent concerns

research.summary: After the 51% controversy, GHash.io publicly pledged steps intended to limit its share and called for industry discussion around mining concentration.
research.significance: The response showed that Bitcoin's social governance could pressure a dominant pool even without a protocol-level cap.

events.title: Cloud mining booms as retail users seek exposure to mining

research.summary: Cloud mining expanded as ASIC hardware raised the cost and complexity of home mining.
research.significance: Industry trend rather than one event; specific company launches/failures are stronger candidates.

events.title: Litecoin miners adopt Scrypt ASICs

research.summary: Scrypt ASIC hardware began eroding Litecoin's earlier resistance to specialized mining.
research.significance: Technological trend relevant to mining history, but current row lacks one clean event/date.

events.title: ChangeTip popularizes tiny Bitcoin tips across social platforms

research.summary: ChangeTip launched a web tipping page in July 2014 and expanded Bitcoin tipping integrations across social platforms during the year.
research.significance: ChangeTip helped make tiny social Bitcoin payments part of early crypto culture.

events.title: Vitalik receives Thiel Fellowship

research.summary: Vitalik Buterin received a Thiel Fellowship in 2014, giving him funding and visibility while building Ethereum.
research.significance: Important founder-development context but needs a primary fellowship announcement URL before final verification.

events.title: Jed McCaleb leaves Ripple and helps launch Stellar

research.summary: Jed McCaleb left Ripple and co-founded Stellar in 2014.
research.significance: The strongest canonical event is Stellar's launch; retain this as founder-lineage context.

events.title: Jed McCaleb's XRP sale plans trigger market controversy

research.summary: Jed McCaleb's plans to sell portions of his XRP holdings became a source of market and governance controversy after his departure from Ripple.
research.significance: Relevant Ripple founder lore, but needs a primary post/legal agreement before standalone scoring.

events.title: Nick Szabo becomes a recurring Satoshi-candidate subject in media

research.summary: Nick Szabo repeatedly appeared in media speculation over Satoshi Nakamoto's identity.
research.significance: Recurring theory rather than a single event; specific investigative publications would be cleaner candidates.

events.title: Silk Road 2.0 is taken down

research.summary: US authorities announced charges against Blake Benthall and the seizure of Silk Road 2.0 in November 2014.
research.significance: The takedown showed that successor darknet markets were also vulnerable to infiltration and law-enforcement seizure.

sources.title: US DOJ — Operator of Silk Road 2.0 charged

events.title: Mt Gox recovery finds roughly 200000 BTC in an old wallet

research.summary: Mt. Gox later disclosed it had found 199,999.99 BTC in an old-format wallet, discovered on 7 March after initially reporting much larger losses.
research.significance: The rediscovery made the already chaotic collapse even stranger and fed years of creditor and forensic scrutiny.

events.title: US court imposes penalties in Bitcoin Savings and Trust case

research.summary: A US federal court entered final judgment against Trendon Shavers and Bitcoin Savings & Trust, ordering more than $40 million in disgorgement and interest plus civil penalties.
research.significance: It was a landmark ruling applying securities law to a Bitcoin-denominated Ponzi scheme.

sources.title: SEC — final judgment against Trendon Shavers / BTCST

events.title: Paycoin and GAW Miners become symbols of mining-related crypto fraud

research.summary: GAW Miners promoted Hashlets and announced Paycoin in November 2014; later federal proceedings found founder Josh Garza had defrauded customers through the mining and virtual-currency businesses.
research.significance: GAW/Paycoin became one of the defining mining-investment fraud stories of the 2014-15 era.

sources.title: US District Court — GAW Miners / Paycoin findings

events.title: Blockchain.info wallet becomes one of the world's most-used Bitcoin wallets

research.summary: Blockchain.info was one of the most widely used web wallets during early Bitcoin adoption.
research.significance: Adoption trend rather than one dated milestone; use a sourced wallet-count milestone if needed for a card.

events.title: Electrum establishes lightweight Bitcoin wallet model

research.summary: Electrum was created by Thomas Voegtlin in November 2011, not 2014.
research.significance: Electrum established a durable lightweight non-custodial wallet model without requiring users to download the full blockchain.

events.title: BIP39 mnemonic seed standard is proposed

research.summary: BIP39 was assigned on 10 September 2013, not 2014, specifying mnemonic sentences for generating deterministic-wallet seeds.
research.significance: BIP39's seed-word format became one of the most recognizable self-custody standards in crypto.

events.title: CryptoNote whitepaper influences privacy-coin development

research.summary: CryptoNote's protocol ideas and whitepaper predated Monero's 2014 launch and influenced Bytecoin/Monero privacy design.
research.significance: This belongs earlier in the privacy lineage rather than as a generic 2014 event.
research.notes: Needs direct CryptoNote paper/archive for exact date.

events.title: Bytecoin controversy drives community interest toward Monero

research.summary: Monero emerged amid controversy around earlier CryptoNote/Bytecoin distribution and was launched as a fair, pre-announced fork of the reference code.
research.significance: This is origin context under the canonical Monero launch rather than a standalone event.

events.title: Mt. Gox collapses

research.summary: Mt. Gox went offline on 25 February 2014 after halting Bitcoin withdrawals earlier in the month and filed for bankruptcy protection in Tokyo on 28 February.
research.significance: The failure of the world's former dominant Bitcoin exchange became crypto's defining early custody and counterparty disaster.

sources.title: The Guardian — MtGox collapse / withdrawal halt analysis

events.title: Ether crowdsale begins

research.summary: Ethereum launched its 42-day Ether genesis sale on 22 July 2014, accepting Bitcoin and initially offering 2,000 ETH per BTC.
research.significance: The crowdsale funded Ethereum's development and became a landmark precursor to the later ICO era.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Launching the Ether Sale
Ethereum Foundation — Ether Sale statistical overview

events.title: Sidechains paper and Blockstream drive Bitcoin scaling research

research.summary: The foundational pegged-sidechains paper was dated 22 October 2014, not 2015.
research.significance: Sidechains proposed moving Bitcoin-linked assets between separate blockchains, shaping later Bitcoin scaling and interoperability systems.

sources.title: Blockstream — Enabling Blockchain Innovations with Pegged Sidechains
